title: Agent Planning, Reflection & Dynamic Replanning
description: Implement Plan-and-Solve architectures, hierarchical task decomposition, reflection critique loops, and dynamic replanning in .NET.

data.text: Why Autonomous Agents Fail Without Planning

When presented with complex, multi-stage enterprise tasks—such as migrating a legacy microservice, reconciling disparate accounting ledgers, or performing an IT security audit—standard reactive agents fail. They exhibit 'greedy action bias': jumping immediately into executing the first tool that comes to mind without scoping prerequisites, getting caught in dead-end loops, or losing sight of the overarching goal after three tool invocations.

data.caption: The Plan-and-Solve Architecture with Reflection and Dynamic Replanning
data.definition:
graph TD
    Goal["User Objective: 'Perform quarterly compliance audit on database X'"] --> Planner["1. Planner Model: Generate DAG of Action Steps"]
    Planner --> PlanReview["Review & State Initialization"]
    PlanReview --> StepExec["2. Executor: Run Current Step Tools"]
    StepExec --> StepResult["Tool Output Recorded"]
    StepResult --> Evaluator["3. Reflector: Evaluate Success of Step"]
    Evaluator --> Decision{Did step succeed & is goal met?}
    Decision -->|Yes, more steps remain| StepExec
    Decision -->|Unexpected error / blocker| Replanner["4. Replanner: Update Remaining Steps"]
    Replanner --> StepExec
    Decision -->|All steps successfully verified| FinalAudit["5. Deliver Comprehensive Audited Result"]

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Unplanned agents succumb to greedy action bias and infinite circular loops
The Plan-and-Solve pattern breaks complex goals into verifiable milestones before action
Dynamic replanning re-evaluates remaining tasks when tool observations reveal unexpected obstacles
Reflection critique passes dramatically reduce hallucinations in customer-facing outputs
Persist the execution plan in durable storage so interrupted long-running workflows can resume seamlessly
data.takeaway: Planning elevates agents from reactive tool-callers to deliberate problem solvers. Structuring workflows into Plan -> Execute -> Reflect -> Replan ensures enterprise predictability.
